newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann set to outline DBKom strategy.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann set to outline DBKom strategy.

text.p: German engineering group Mannesmann on Thursday will take the wrappings off its communications venture with the German railway, giving it a new name and laying out its strategy to compete against Deutsche Telekom.

Mannesmann took out glossy advertisements in leading German newspapers on Wednesday giving an indication that part of its strategy will be to stress that customers in the past have had no alternative to phone service from monopoly Telekom.
"Until now, telecommunications was a very one-sided affair...we're going to play a different tune," the company said in two-page advertisement signed by "The Telephone People".

The venture is currently called DBKom GmbH and was formed last year when a consortium led by Mannesmann that includes U.S. phone giant AT&T and the European Unisource alliance bought 49.8 percent of the German railway's telecoms unit.

It merges the railway's communications networks with Mannesmann's Communications Network International to create Germany's second-largest carrier after Deutsche Telekom, with annual sales estimated at over a billion marks ($609 million).

Mannesmann operates the D2 mobile phone group, Germany's leading digital cellular network, which includes a microwave network of 35,000 km (21,750 miles) that would complement the DBKom's 40,000 km communications network along the railway lines.
While in need of modernisation, it is Germany's largest phone network after Deutsche Telekom.
Industry analysts hope Mannesmann will provide more financial details about the deal to determine what impact future investment will have on the engineering group's profits.

When it announced the deal in July, Mannesmann and railway Deutsche Bahn AG gave very few details about the venture, declining to say how much the stake was sold for or how it would enter the market when competition takes off next year.

"We would like to hear a concrete statement about how much the deal cost, when it will be profitable and how this will affect Mannesmann earnings," said Eggert Kuls, an equities analyst with investment bank M.M. Warburg in Hamburg.

Although it has not revealed financial details of the deal, Mannesmann board member Peter Mihatsch has said the group would invest three to four billion marks over the next four years and to be profitable in two and a half to three years.

Mannesmann's consortium has an option to increase its stake in DBKom to 74.9 percent within three years. The diversified German group controls 70 percent of the consortium, compared with 15 percent each for AT&T and Unisource.
Separately, Mannesmann operates the D2 digital cellular phone network, Germany's leading mobile phone service, and has entered a number of international telecoms ventures.
The involvement of AT&T Corp will give the DBKom venture a global outlet, which is crucial for business communications, as well as the contribution of AT&T's marketing know-how.
Unisource is a business communications provider owned by PTT Nederland, Telia of Sweden, Swiss Telecom PTT and Spain's Telefonica.

Together AT&T and Unisource operate a joint venture called AT&T/Unisource, which offers communications services for corporations and says it has become Europe's largest provider of Internet services for buisinesses.
